title: Bin Ren – text2quant (S7E2)

reader_summary.headline: All opinions expressed by podcast participants are solely their own opinion.
reader_summary.overview: All opinions expressed by podcast participants are solely their own opinion. and do not reflect the opinion of newfound research. In this episode, I speak with Bin Ren, founder of SigTech, a financial technology platform providing quantitative researchers with access to a state-of-of-of-the-art analysis engine.

key_points.text: This conversation is really broken into two parts.
key_points.evidence_quote: This conversation is really broken into two parts.

key_points.text: In the first half, we discuss BIN's views on designing and developing a state-of-the-art back-art back-art back-testing engine.
key_points.evidence_quote: In the first half, we discuss BIN's views on designing and developing a state-of-the-art back-art back-art back-testing engine.

key_points.text: This includes concepts around monolithic versus modular design, how tightly coupled the engine should be.
key_points.evidence_quote: This includes concepts around monolithic versus modular design, how tightly coupled the engine should be, and the blurred line between where a strategy definition ends and the back-testing engine begins.

key_points.text: In the second half of the conversation.
key_points.evidence_quote: In the second half of the conversation, we discussed the significant pivot SIGTech has undergone this year to incorporate large language models into its process, or perhaps more accurately, allow large language models into its process.

thesis: The episode discusses the history of cloud computing, specifically the development of the Zen virtualization technology at Cambridge University and its adoption by Amazon's AWS. It also outlines the structure of the podcast conversation, which covers designing quantitative back-testing engines and the integration of large language models into financial technology processes.
